nodes.characterization_summary: In situ XRD patterns of Ni(OH)2/NF show appearance of strong peaks assigned to γ-NiOOH confirming its existence at certain potentials.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando XPS of Co0.8Fe0.2P@C shows increasing Co^{3+} and M-O peaks with decaying P peak, confirming formation of active CoOOH with P leaching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the intensity increasing trend of the XPS peaks assigned to Co^{3+} and M-O along with the decay of P peak in operando XPS spectra of Co_{0.8}Fe_{0.2}P@C during electrochemical activation, confirming the formation of active CoOOH species accompanied with the leaching of P.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman of NiFe2O4/NF shows peaks at 474 and 554 cm^{-1} assigned to γ-NiOOH appearing at 1.41 V vs RHE, indicating Ni^{3+} formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman peaks at 474 and 554 cm^{-1} could be assigned to γ -NiOOH , which would appear as the potential increased to 1.41 V , indicating the formation of Ni^{3 + } active species on the surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ XANES of Li2Co2O4 shows positive shift/decreased intensity of Co K-edge after OER indicating increased Co valence; FT-EXAFS shows Co-O distance shrinkage and Debye-Waller factor increase confirming CoO6 octahedron distortion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a positive shift and decreased intensity of Co K-edge XANE spectra after the OER, indicating an increase in the cobalt valence state. Moreover, the variation of Co K-edge EXAFS spectra reflects the shrinkage of Co-O distance and increasing Debye-Waller factor, confirming a distortion of the CoO_6 octahedron.
